gen-gf-bellota-text-work-sans: Bellota Text brings open, unshaded letterforms and a distinctive presence. The standout is the height gap: Work Sans stands tall on its high mean line while the heading's lowercase stays moderate.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-archivo: Archivo has outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height, friendly and editorial. Bruno Ace adds a ruler-drawn, constant-width line and a lingering rhythm, so the text beneath keeps moving at a quicker pace.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-asap: Distinctive and expressive, Bruno Ace looks ruler-drawn, curves and straights sharing a width. Asap, a readable sans-serif whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals, can go slightly smaller than you'd expect.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Be Vietnam Pro reads clean, with curve endings that never crowd each other. Bruno Ace is best at being noticed, with its ruler-drawn line and connected counters, while Be Vietnam Pro is best at carrying words quietly.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-epilogue: Approachable and contemporary, Epilogue is a plain sans with curvy, tall-bodied letters and stubby ascenders. But Bruno Ace holds a ruler-straight, constant line, so the page moves between a lingering heading and looser text.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-fira-sans: Bruno Ace draws its lines with a ruler's constancy, leaving counters connected to the outside. Fira Sans, with its larger-than-usual x-height and no thick-thin contrast, would loom if enlarged beside that heading.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans stands tall, making words look sturdy and large. Bruno Ace excels at its unshifting, ruler-drawn line with no weight change on any curve, while Merriweather Sans excels at an e that opens clearly.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-public-sans: A ruler-drawn, constant-width line makes Bruno Ace instantly recognizable, its counters connected to the outside. Public Sans already has a hefty lowercase, so it can stay modest in size.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-ranade: Bruno Ace keeps a single stroke weight throughout, which makes it distinctive. It does display best, with no stroke contrast at all, while Ranade does text best, with a restrained thick-thin rhythm and widely spaced type.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-supreme: Crisp, heavy, ruler-straight: Bruno Ace's constant line meets Supreme. Supreme, a sans-serif with a heavy-looking band of text and letters held open, should read crisply and steadily across many lines.
